title: 2026 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont's at-large congressional district
description: The 2026 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the state's sole at-large congressional representative. Incumbent Democrat Becca Balint, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024, is seeking a third term. She faces a Republican primary contest between Mark Coester, a small-business owner who challenged her in 2024, and Gerald Malloy, a West Point graduate and combat veteran who has previously run for U.S. Senate. Vermont is a heavily Democratic state that has not elected a Republican to this seat since 1988, making Balint the strong favorite in the general election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this specific race as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the seat as Safe Democratic.

candidates.name: Becca Balint
candidates.summary: Becca Balint is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Vermont's at-large congressional district, first elected in 2022. She is the first woman and openly LGBTQ+ person to represent Vermont in Congress. Before her election to the U.S. House, Balint served in the Vermont Senate from 2015 to 2023, including as President pro tempore. She is running for re-election on a platform of protecting reproductive rights, limiting corporate influence in politics, and opposing the Trump administration's policies.

candidates.name: Mark Coester
candidates.summary: Mark Coester is a small-business owner, logger, and maple syrup producer from Westminster, Vermont, running for the Republican nomination for U.S. House. He was the Republican nominee in 2024, receiving 30% of the vote against incumbent Becca Balint. Coester emphasizes conservative positions on border security, energy independence, term limits, and reducing federal overreach. He has been making maple syrup in Vermont for over 50 years and operates a small business.

candidates.name: Gerald Malloy
candidates.summary: Gerald Malloy is a West Point graduate, combat veteran, and business owner who has entered the Republican primary for Vermont's U.S. House seat. He previously ran for U.S. Senate in Vermont in 2022 and 2024, challenging independent Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Senator Peter Welch. Malloy campaigns on a platform of bringing a results-oriented approach to Congress, working with the Trump administration to deliver for Vermont, and lowering the political temperature in Washington.

forecast.rationale: No public polls are available for this race, so confidence is limited and based on fundamentals rather than direct voter data. Still, the available race information strongly favors Democrats: incumbent Becca Balint is seeking a third term, Vermont is described here as a heavily Democratic state, Republicans have not won this at-large House seat since 1988, and the 2024 Republican nominee Mark Coester received only 30% against Balint. The race description explicitly calls Balint the strong favorite, and the Cook Political Report rating of Safe Democratic aligns with that assessment. Given the absence of polling, some uncertainty remains, but the overall evidence supports an overwhelming Democratic advantage in the general election.
